NDT training in West Virginia: how it works for West Virginia employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for West Virginia employers and technicians live online or onsite at your facility, whether that is a Kanawha Valley chemical plant, a Marcellus gas-processing site or an Ohio Valley fabrication shop. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer then certifies you under its own written practice.

That last point matters more in West Virginia than most people expect. Under SNT-TC-1A there is no state-issued or ASNT-issued NDT licence that you carry from job to job. The certificate a chemical plant contractor in Institute or a pipeline inspection company in Bridgeport accepts is the one its own written practice produces: documented training, documented experience, exams given under a Level III, and a current vision test. Training is the first building block. It is not the certificate itself, and any provider who says otherwise is overselling.

We also want to be clear about something the geography of the state makes obvious. Atlantis has no training centre in Charleston, Morgantown, Wheeling, Parkersburg or anywhere else in West Virginia. We do not need one. Theory runs as live virtual sessions that technicians join from home, a hotel room or the site office. Practical work happens onsite at the employer's facility, on the employer's equipment and on specimens that look like the welds, castings and corroded piping the crew actually examines. For a state where a drive from the Northern Panhandle to the southern coalfields can take most of a day on two-lane roads, bringing the instructor to the crew nearly always costs less in lost hours than sending the crew somewhere.

If you already know what you need, request a West Virginia training quote. We send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in West Virginia

Every course below is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is taught so that your written practice can accept it. How many classroom hours each method and level needs is set out in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice may ask for more than the SNT-TC-1A recommendation, never less, so check the matrix against your own document before you book.

MethodLevelsWhat West Virginia employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic thickness and shear wave)I, II, III prepWall-loss surveys on Kanawha Valley process piping, shear-wave weld examination in fabrication shops, boiler tube and header thickness at coal- and gas-fired stationsNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepWeld examination on new-build gas-processing piping, corrosion mapping on vessels, girth welds on transmission and gathering linesUT Level II, or conventional UT knowledge the written practice accepts
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, III prepThick-section weld sizing on pressure vessels and heavy wall piping, often run alongside PAUTUT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds to API 1104, ASME Section VIII vessel seams, B31.3 process piping in chemical plantsNone for Level I; radiation-safety training and radiographer certification are separate legal requirements (see below)
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepStructural steel and bridge welds, crane and mining-equipment components, pipeline dig sites, rotating-equipment shaftsNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless and nickel-alloy piping in chemical service, non-magnetic castings, weld root checksNone for Level I
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection to AWS D1.1 and D1.5, in-service visual on tanks, vessels and structures, pre- and post-weld fit-up checksNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection at power stations and chemical plants, surface crack detection on coated weldsNone for Level I

UT. The UT course starts with the physics of sound in steel: velocity, wavelength, attenuation and mode conversion. It then moves to instrument calibration on reference blocks, straight-beam thickness work and angle-beam weld examination with distance-amplitude correction. At Level II the focus moves to interpreting indications against the acceptance criteria your contracts name. For a West Virginia chemical plant that usually means ASME B31.3. For a pressure-vessel shop it means ASME Section VIII. At an electric utility it means the station's own boiler and piping programme.

PAUT and TOFD. These are advanced UT techniques and they come after conventional UT, not before it. The courses cover probe and wedge selection, focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, and TOFD's dead zones and sizing geometry. They also cover data analysis, which is the part employers care about most. As more gas-processing and transmission work in the state is examined with encoded ultrasonics in place of film, a PAUT Level II has become one of the more marketable qualifications a UT technician here can add.

RT. The RT course covers radiation sources and X-ray tubes, exposure calculation, film and digital detectors, image quality indicators, geometric unsharpness and interpretation of weld discontinuities. We teach interpretation against API 1104 for pipeline work and ASME Section V and VIII for vessels. The radiation-safety side is a separate legal requirement. It is explained in the regulator section below because West Virginia's position on this is unusual.

MT and PT. The surface methods are short courses, and they are often the first certifications a new hire earns. MT covers magnetisation techniques (yoke, prod, coil, central conductor), wet and dry particles, fluorescent versus visible, field direction and demagnetisation. PT covers penetrant types and methods, dwell times, developer application, temperature limits and how to tell relevant indications from false ones. On a mixed chemical-plant scope, a technician with MT and PT Level II plus VT is useful from the first day.

VT. Visual testing is underrated, and in structural and bridge work it is the method that finds most problems. The course covers direct and remote visual, lighting and access, weld profile gauges, and acceptance criteria from AWS D1.1 (structural steel) and D1.5 (bridges). It also covers how visual findings should be documented so they hold up in an audit.

ET. Eddy current covers impedance-plane analysis, probe types, frequency selection and calibration standards. It also covers the tube-inspection applications that make ET valuable at power stations and chemical plants with large heat-exchanger populations. Surface-array and weld-probe techniques for crack detection through coatings are included where the employer needs them.

Level III preparation. For experienced Level IIs aiming to become the person who writes procedures and qualifies others, the ASNT Level III programme covers the Basic exam (materials, processes, other methods, and SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 themselves) and method-specific preparation. You sit the ASNT Level III exams through ASNT, not through us.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in West Virginia, step by step

  1. Find out whose written practice you will be certified under. Your employer's written practice is the controlling document. It sets the training hours, experience hours, exam format, passing grades and recertification interval for each method and level. If you are job-hunting rather than employed, pick the method your target employers use most (usually UT or MT/PT in this state) and train in that first.
  2. Complete the classroom training. Formal training hours for each method and level, delivered live online or onsite, with attendance and content documented. Our training-requirements matrix lists the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours so you can compare them with your written practice.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Experience hours are logged in the method, under qualified supervision, and properly documented. This is where most West Virginia candidates lose time. The hours happen in the field, but nobody writes them down in a form an auditor will accept. Keep a signed log from the start.
  4. Pass the general exam. A written exam on the principles of the method, taken under the supervision of a Level III.
  5. Pass the specific exam. A written exam on the procedures, codes, equipment and acceptance criteria your employer actually uses: B31.3, Section VIII, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or whatever the written practice names.
  6. Pass the practical exam. A hands-on exam on real specimens with real flaws, set and graded by a Level III. Under SNT-TC-1A the three exam grades are combined into a composite, and your written practice sets the passing marks.
  7. Pass the vision examination. A near-vision acuity check and a colour-contrast check. The near-vision check is repeated at least annually.
  8. Receive certification from your employer. The employer certifies you in writing, based on the records above. Records stay on file and are what a client or auditor will ask to see.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Recertification follows the interval in the written practice (SNT-TC-1A recommends no more than five years), and certification can lapse if you stop working in the method. When you change employers, your new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, although it may credit your documented training and experience.

For the complete framework, see our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for West Virginia crews

There are three ways to run a programme for a West Virginia team. We will tell you honestly which one fits.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions with real-time questions, worked examples and quizzes. This is how most individuals and small crews cover the classroom portion. It suits technicians who rotate between sites in the Marcellus and Utica counties and cannot be pulled off a job for a full week. Details are on the online NDT training page.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-supervised programme delivered at your plant, shop or yard, using your instruments and your specimens. For a chemical-plant contractor in the Kanawha Valley or an inspection company in the I-79 corridor, this usually works best. The crew stays close to the work, the practical matches the actual scope, and the specific exam can be written around your actual procedures.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a concentrated onsite practical block. This is often the most efficient route for multi-method programmes.

Scheduling in West Virginia follows the work calendar. Coal- and gas-fired stations along the Ohio and Kanawha rivers take planned outages, often in spring and autumn, when inspection demand peaks and nobody is free for a classroom. Chemical-plant turnarounds do the same. Pipeline construction slows in the mountains in deep winter. We plan cohorts so the training finishes before your crew is needed. Practical sessions can be booked into the gaps between turnarounds, and theory can run in the evenings during a busy spell. For larger groups, corporate NDT training explains how multi-method, multi-site programmes are sequenced so the crew keeps working while it qualifies.

What we will not do is pretend a practical exam can be done over video. It cannot. Theory can be remote. The hands-on qualification cannot. Ask about onsite training for your West Virginia crew.

Where NDT technicians work in West Virginia

Demand for NDT technicians in West Virginia comes from a handful of heavy industries. Each has its own codes and its own expectations of a technician.

The Kanawha Valley chemical corridor. The chemical plants strung along the Kanawha River around Charleston, including Institute, South Charleston, Nitro and Belle, have processed chemicals for generations. That means a lot of ageing process piping, vessels and heat exchangers under mechanical-integrity programmes. The core work is UT thickness and corrosion monitoring, PT on stainless and alloy systems, VT, and ET on exchanger bundles. ASME B31.3 governs process piping. In-service vessel and piping programmes are usually written around API 510 and API 570, and some employers also ask their inspectors to hold those API certifications. Atlantis does not train for those schemes. What we provide is the SNT-TC-1A method certification that the NDT itself needs.

Marcellus and Utica gas: gathering, processing and transmission. Northern and north-central West Virginia (Marshall, Wetzel, Doddridge, Harrison and neighbouring counties) is where shale gas is gathered, processed and compressed. Large gas-processing and fractionation complexes need NDT during construction and throughout operation. Pipelines are examined to API 1104. Transmission and gathering lines fall under federal pipeline safety rules (49 CFR Parts 192 and 195), which require qualified welding and NDT. Operator qualification for covered tasks is a separate requirement from NDT certification, and pipeline operators check both. The Mountain Valley Pipeline, which starts in north-central West Virginia, is one recent example of the transmission build-out that has kept RT and AUT crews busy.

Power generation. West Virginia still has large coal-fired stations, including several along the Ohio and Kanawha rivers and around Morgantown, as well as gas-fired units. Boilers and high-energy piping are built and repaired to ASME Section I and B31.1. During outages there is steady demand for UT thickness on waterwalls and headers, MT and PT on attachments and welds, and ET on condenser and feedwater-heater tubes.

Steel and heavy fabrication. The steel industry is growing again, with new mill capacity in the Ohio Valley and the Eastern Panhandle. There is also a long-standing network of fabrication, machine and mining-equipment shops. Their work is structural welding to AWS D1.1, pressure-vessel fabrication to ASME Section VIII, and MT/PT on castings and forgings.

Bridges and highways. West Virginia has a large inventory of steel bridges on a mountainous road network, so bridge inspection and bridge fabrication are a real employer base. Fabrication follows AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, with UT, MT and VT as the main methods. In-service steel bridge inspection uses VT, MT, PT and UT on fracture-critical members.

Radiography licensing in West Virginia. This is the question we are asked most. West Virginia has historically been a non-Agreement State. Radioactive materials such as the iridium-192 and selenium-75 sources used in gamma radiography have therefore been licensed by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, through NRC Region I, rather than by the state. The state regulates X-ray equipment. In 2024 the Legislature passed a law to begin the transfer to Agreement State status under a state radiation programme in the Department of Health. Before mobilising a radiography crew, check the current position with the NRC and the state, because licensing authority may move during the transition. Whichever agency holds the licence, industrial radiographers must hold radiographer certification (under 10 CFR Part 34 or the equivalent state rule, typically through the ASNT Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme or a recognised state programme) and must work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification shows you can produce and interpret radiographs. It does not authorise you to handle a source. You need both.

What local employers ask for. Across these sectors, West Virginia job postings most often ask for ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, MT and PT. RT Level II and radiographer certification are wanted for pipeline and vessel work. Advanced-UT roles ask for PAUT or TOFD. Some postings also list CWI, API 510/570/653 or ISO 9712. Those are separate schemes that the employer or the candidate arranges through their own bodies. For typical pay by level, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for West Virginia NDT companies

Many West Virginia inspection companies are small. A handful of Level IIs serve pipeline, plant and fabrication clients, and there is no full-time Level III on staff. SNT-TC-1A still requires a written practice. It requires exams to be given by a qualified Level III. It requires records a client auditor can follow. An ASME Section VIII fabricator's quality manual also expects NDE personnel to be qualified to a written practice. Atlantis supports these employers directly:

  • Written-practice development and review. We draft a new written practice or bring an old one up to date for the methods and levels you actually use, aligned with the current SNT-TC-1A and with what your clients' specifications demand. See NDT written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Exam administration, procedure writing and approval, technique sheets, and review of the certification records you already hold. This works well when you have just won a contract whose specification needs Level III sign-off you don't have in house.
  • Audit preparation. Before a client audit or a code-stamp review, we check training, experience, vision and exam records against your written practice and flag gaps while there is still time to close them.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. Our SNT-TC-1A certification page explains the employer-based model in plain language for managers who do not come from an NDT background.

If that describes your company, book a Level III consultation and tell us which methods, how many technicians and which client specifications apply.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam is where most first-time candidates struggle. Usually the reason is not the physics. They have not handled enough set-ups under pressure. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. A West Virginia technician can use it to rehearse scan patterns, calibration sequences and indication recognition between sessions, including the plant and tank scenarios that match much of the state's work.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace hands-on training on real instruments, and it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens with real flaws, which your written practice requires. Treat it as extra repetitions, not a short cut.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, the exam structure and the practical assessments. Onsite programmes run under that Level III oversight, so the training records, exam records and procedures a West Virginia employer receives are produced to a single consistent standard.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in West Virginia

How do I get NDT certified in West Virginia?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, you are certified by your employer, not by the state. You complete classroom training for the method and level, log supervised on-the-job experience, and pass general, specific and practical exams given under a Level III, plus a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis provides the training and, for employers who need it, the Level III and written-practice support.

Can I take NDT training online in West Virginia?

Yes, for the theory. Live online sessions cover the classroom hours for most methods, which suits technicians spread across the state. Practical training and the practical exam must be done hands-on with real equipment and specimens, either onsite at your employer's facility or in a scheduled practical block. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours and experience hours your employer's written practice requires, and on whether you are starting from zero or already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums for both. Our training-requirements matrix lists them by method and level. In practice, the experience hours take longer than the classroom, so start a documented log as early as you can.

Do I need a license for radiography in West Virginia?

Yes, but not an NDT licence. Radioactive sources for gamma radiography must be held under a radioactive materials licence. West Virginia has historically been under NRC jurisdiction for these and is moving toward Agreement State status, so check the current licensing authority. Every radiographer must also hold radiographer certification and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate requirement that covers technique and interpretation.

What does NDT training cost in West Virginia?

We do not publish prices, because the cost depends on the method, the level, the group size and whether the programme is online, onsite or blended. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a West Virginia training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by West Virginia employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for NDT personnel certification among US inspection companies, fabricators, utilities and chemical plants, and it is referenced by codes such as ASME Section VIII. Because certification is employer-based, a new employer will re-certify you under its own written practice, usually crediting your documented training and experience.

Which NDT method should I learn first to work in West Virginia?

For most entry-level roles, start with MT, PT and VT (short courses with broad use) and add UT. If you are aiming at pipeline construction, RT together with radiographer certification is the traditional entry point. More and more jobs also ask for encoded UT, so plan a route toward PAUT once you hold UT Level II.

Do you train for API 510, 570 or 653, or CWI?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some West Virginia employers, particularly chemical plants and tank owners, also ask for API inspector certifications or CWI. Those are separate schemes with their own bodies and exams. Our training covers the NDT method certifications that sit alongside them.

Can you train our crew onsite at our plant or shop in West Virginia?

Yes. Onsite delivery at the employer's facility is our standard model for crews. Practicals use your instruments and specimens, and the specific exam can reflect your own procedures. Ask about onsite training for your West Virginia crew.

Can you schedule training around a plant outage or turnaround?

Yes. We plan cohorts around outage and turnaround windows, so training finishes before the crew is needed or fits into the quiet weeks afterwards. Theory can also run in the evenings during busy periods.

Our company has no Level III. Can you help?

Yes. We provide outsourced Level III services: written-practice development, exam administration, procedure approval and record review. See written practice development and Level III training if you want to develop your own Level III over time.

How do I prepare for the UT Level 2 exam?

Work through the method theory, then practise calibration and scanning until the set-up is second nature. Use mock questions such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and rehearse on the Practical NDT simulator before the real practical exam.
